narrative:
The model estimated a 34.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. Under the lender’s risk policy, that was high enough to deny the application; it does not mean default is certain, only that the assessed risk exceeded the approval cutoff.

The most influential factor was your requested credit amount of 2,039 DM, and it worked in your favor because it is below the approved applicants’ average of about 3,020 DM. The second most important factor was your checking-account status of 0–200 DM, and it counted against you: most approved applicants had no checking-account information listed, while only about 18% were in your range. The third most important factor was your one year at your present residence, which slightly helped your case, though it is shorter than the approved average of about three years. Overall, your lower requested amount and residence history helped, but the checking-account status was a meaningful warning sign, and the combined picture led to denial.

To improve a future application, focus on building a stronger checking-account history—avoid overdrafts and maintain a positive balance record—and consider applying after a longer period at your current address. You may also ask the lender whether updated income, savings, or a guarantor/co-applicant could be considered.
